methodology_reference.use: educational/autocall mechanics reference, not note-level outcome data

findings: Nasdaq exposes discoverable listed autocallable note securities and identifiers.
The sampled pages did not provide usable bid/ask or historical time series; displayed status was data not available.
Nasdaq sample is complementary to Leonteq terms pages but not a replacement for termsheets or verified settlements.
next_experiment: Use Nasdaq identifiers to search issuer prospectus/SEC filings and exchange notices, then require independent settlement evidence before labels.

objections: No verifiable market data (bid/ask x or 'data not available')
No shared ISINs with known issuers (Leonteq/SEC) for cross-verification
Pilot pages lack production labels or usage context
Educational article alone does not validate structured-product mechanics
acceptance_tests: Verify bid/ask spreads via alternative data sources (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters)
Cross-check ISINs against Nasdaq’s official structured-products registry
Confirm pilot pages are non-production (e.g., test environment flags)
Replicate autocall mechanics using the Nasdaq article’s formulas
review.next_experiment: Query Nasdaq directly for pilot metadata (e.g., ISINs, issuance dates) and request sample trade data
safety_flags: No regulatory disclosures (SEC/Prospectus) linked to ISINs
Pilot pages may be placeholder templates without live pricing
Educational content does not substitute for actual product terms

acceptance_tests: educational source separated from note outcomes
